title: Formation of Lake Baikal
summary: Around twenty-five million years ago during the Late Oligocene, tectonic rifting tore open the Baikal Rift Zone across southern Siberia. Crustal subsidence created an immense continental graben that filled with freshwater, developing into Lake Baikal. As the deepest lake on Earth at 1,642 meters and holding one-fifth of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater, Baikal preserves a continuous twenty-five-million-year sedimentary climate archive and sustains an extraordinary ecosystem dominated by endemic species.

uncertainty.note: Rifting in the Baikal depression began in the Late Oligocene, approximately 25 to 30 million years ago, creating an active continental rift system that continues to subside and deepen today (USGS; UNESCO).

as_recorded.value: oldest (25 million years) and deepest (1,700 m) lake in the world
perhaps more than 25 million years old, the oldest as well

where.historical_name: Baikal rift depression, southern Siberia, Late Oligocene; no polities existed

importance.justification: Earth's oldest and deepest freshwater lake, containing 20% of the planet's unfrozen surface freshwater in an active continental rift.
